title: KIPC Resource Audit
subtitle: Boundedness, ownership, synchronization and adversarial qualification
status: Audit and proposed correction; production implementation not changed

defects.title: Outbound mailbox and writer retention
defects.finding: WorkerLink posts without admission; WriteQueue retains payload closures without byte or message caps. A no-read synthetic peer accepted 512 x 64 KiB. An injected stalled writer retained 2,048 payloads / 128 MiB. The active-write timeout begins at service, so it cannot cap producer bursts or queue age.
defects.correction: One ledger before the first retention; finite bytes, records and residence time; no admission waiters.

defects.title: Pre-Ready work escapes a Worker-only limit
defects.finding: FS encodes before its first await; invokeFs/invokeAuth then await whenReady. Each whenReady can add a promise/waiter. A healthy link that never sends Ready can retain any number of encoded requests. Moving admission only into WorkerLink leaves this path untouched.
defects.correction: Reserve at the public adapter before encoding or readiness retention. Preserve direct whenReady semantics; refuse excess operation records locally.

defects.title: Active CALL state has no aggregate bound
defects.finding: Main creates a timer, Promise and Map record per call. Worker creates its own pending record. The 256-abandoned cap acts only after timeouts are processed; it does not bound active calls or a burst before that point. A peer can drain writes and withhold replies while byte use stays low.
defects.correction: Keep one operation record until caller settlement AND Worker pending/tombstone retirement AND terminal delivery. Bound tombstone retirement separately.

defects.title: Inbound ring drains into unbounded handlers
defects.finding: The ring releases a CALL before startCallHandler. A real socket probe with eight ring slots started 512 unresolved handlers. After close, all 512 continuations resumed when their barrier opened; late answers were suppressed. Closing a transport does not cancel arbitrary application promises.
defects.correction: Reserve handler count, input retention and maximum answer bytes before invoking application code; prevent further invocation on exhaustion.

defects.title: Host acknowledges an unbounded UI backlog
defects.finding: One window produced 4,096 Accepted replies while 4,096 setter commands remained unconsumed. The registry window/destroy limits are different resources. The wake bridge forwards into Tao, so bounding only the mpsc channel would move retention downstream.
defects.correction: Reserve before enqueue and before Accepted. Transfer the same permit through Tao; release on physical UI consumption or proven discard.

defects.title: Native facts accumulate before filtering
defects.finding: UI observations enqueue four state facts through unbounded mpsc. Changed-only filtering occurs later in Core. The coordinator can wait on the shared writer while native observations continue. Duplicate filtering after the queue cannot bound that queue.
defects.correction: A bounded native-to-Core mailbox with reserved lifecycle capacity. UI must not block. Coalescing requires explicit state-event semantics.

defects.title: Backing storage and shared-input ownership are unpriced
defects.finding: A one-byte Uint8Array view cloned an 8 MiB backing buffer on Bun 1.4.4. SharedArrayBuffer stayed shared and a post-send mutation was visible to the receiver. Direct WriteQueue also sent a later mutation. The low-level immutable-snapshot promise is currently unclear; the alias is demonstrated, not an invented existing API guarantee.
defects.correction: Compact ordinary input after admission; charge copy overlap. Reject shared-backed input or specify a synchronization protocol. Copying an unsynchronized SAB is not a coherent snapshot proof.

defects.title: Codec and reader allocation differ from wire bytes
defects.finding: 262,151 AuthRequest wire bytes decoded into 262,144 empty strings; vector capacity alone was 8,388,480 bytes. The 32-call auth limit is a record bound. FS encoded an over-limit string before rejecting it. FrameReader accounts received fill bytes rather than the allocated fill capacity and copies callbacks before its aggregate check. These are amplification/transient proof gaps, not infinite single-frame allocation claims.
defects.correction: Schema-owned cardinality and decoded-storage limits before allocation; bounded encoder scratch; separately price callback, active fill, owned chunks and decode overlap.

defects.title: Legal FS result cannot fit the default async ring
defects.finding: Native FS permits 8 MiB. Default WorkerLink ring is 1 MiB. An independently encoded valid response for a 2 MiB file had a 2,097,173-byte envelope and failed with KELD-IPC-026 in an otherwise empty default ring. The probe exercised real WorkerLink/UDS, not a real filesystem Host call.
defects.correction: For the API role, provision a ring large enough for its largest legal encoded response, counted globally. With power-of-two rings, an 8 MiB result needs a 16 MiB ring. An alternate reply lane is a larger design.

defects.title: Rust active write lacks an absolute frame clock
defects.finding: write_frame uses write_all(header), write_all(payload), then flush. OS write timeouts constrain individual waits. Repeated successful short writes can outlast the intended frame budget while shared generation/transition locks remain held. A no-read peer does time out. A finite frame is not claimed to make positive progress literally forever.
defects.correction: One absolute header+payload+flush deadline; remaining-time waits; poison after a partial failure. Cancellation/close must not need the lock held by blocked I/O.

defects.title: Queue residence and control fairness have no bound
defects.finding: The writer is FIFO and its five-second clock starts only when a frame becomes active. Control, answers, abandon and close can sit behind admitted data. Reserved admission credit cannot make them overtake existing FIFO work. Strict ordering supplies no independent per-channel latency guarantee.
defects.correction: Preserve FIFO. Add admission-to-service and close deadlines plus bounded admission shares. Do not add a priority queue that changes accepted order.

defects.title: One renderer response can wait without end
defects.finding: The renderer bridge repeats recv_timeout(APP_LINK_READER_POLL) until reply, disconnect or stop. There is no overall response deadline. One pending slot bounds memory but can hold the renderer dispatcher indefinitely while a live Bun handler never answers.
defects.correction: Give the caller an absolute response deadline and bounded late-reply ownership; do not replay an unknown effect.

defects.title: Retired reader metadata grows with session history
defects.finding: Each generation appends a stop Arc and retains its JoinHandle. Retirement defers joins to terminal shutdown to avoid a real guardian acknowledgement deadlock. Spaced restarts can outlive the sliding crash window and grow retained history. This is metadata/result retention, not demonstrated live-thread leakage.
defects.correction: Reap completed retired readers asynchronously outside the dependency cycle. Bound the reaper backlog and stop registrations before admitting more generations.

defects.title: Architecture text can permit unsafe reasoning
defects.finding: Architecture02 equates pending post-Quit 022 with 024, while approved GH527 says 022 means effect unknown and only host 024 proves nonexecution. It also presents remote cancellation and allocation-free calls without accurate Current/Target status. Live timeout merely abandons correlation; it does not cancel queued or remote work.
defects.correction: Correct the exact architecture text, retain typed failure distinctions, and prohibit automatic replay of unanswered calls.

stages.stage: 1. Public producer, generated encoder and readiness
stages.Ownership: Application owns inputs until the adapter snapshots them. Generated FS/auth codecs own serialized payloads. app.ts owns Ready waiters and the singleton link attempt.
stages.Bytes and messages: No aggregate pre-Ready operation/byte cap. Frame limit is 16 MiB after several encoders have allocated. Direct whenReady waiters have no count bound.
stages.Allocation: String UTF-8 buffers, byte snapshots, joined payload, Promise continuations and per-call Ready waiters. Auth vectors create per-element objects/arrays.
stages.Copy count: FS Write normally copies content into encodeBytes, then into joinPayload: two source-visible content copies before posting. UTF-8 encoding is a representation allocation, counted separately.
stages.Backpressure: No feedback from socket or UI consumption reaches this retained pre-Ready work. A singleton connection attempt does not bound its subscribers.
stages.Failure: Local codec errors reject async APIs. Link failure rejects readiness waiters. An authenticated but never-Ready link is a distinct indefinite wait.
stages.Cancellation: No public operation cancellation here. Waiting time before transport call is outside its later call deadline.
stages.Ordering: Snapshot occurs before readiness yields. FIFO guarantees begin at post order, not arbitrary concurrent API invocation order.
stages.Fairness: No producer quota or bounded admission arbitration. Application scheduling determines call order.
stages.Slow peer: Withheld Ready retains requests without requiring a blocked socket. High-rate producers can grow this graph indefinitely.
stages.Crash/restart cleanup: A failed singleton is not reset for reconnect. Failure rejects waiters, but only actual reference retirement and GC reclaim objects.
stages.Evidence: S07-S10, S27; executed oversized-string allocation probe.

stages.Ownership: WorkerLink owns a private MessagePort; Bun owns serialized/in-transit message storage. One FIFO carries data and control.
stages.Bytes and messages: No configured cap. sendEvent posts after per-frame validation. CALLs add main pending state before posting.
stages.Allocation: Message envelope, runtime clone storage, and closure/control metadata. A tiny view can clone a much larger backing store.
stages.Copy count: Ordinary ArrayBuffer input is cloned at this boundary in the executed Bun probe. Exact transient overlap/native storage is not proven. Shared backing aliases rather than snapshots.
stages.Backpressure: postMessage returns void. It does not wait for Worker service or socket drain.
stages.Failure: Synchronous clone/post failure must roll back every reservation and pending record in the future design. Current code has no aggregate capacity failure.
stages.Cancellation: Abandon and close are messages behind earlier posts; they do not remove messages already posted.
stages.Ordering: The captured native port method preserves the existing single outbound FIFO. A second independent queue would create another ordering owner.
stages.Fairness: Data can consume all available runtime queue storage before terminal metadata is serviced. FIFO alone gives no channel share.
stages.Slow peer: Worker can drain the port faster than the socket by moving work into WriteQueue. Neither local queue is bounded.
stages.Crash/restart cleanup: Terminal STATE stops new public work; Worker exit/termination handles transport lifetime. Physical mailbox reclamation must be qualified independently.
stages.Evidence: S03, S05, S28, S34; native UDS flood and backing-store probes.

stages.stage: 3. Worker operation records and local producers
stages.Ownership: TransportWorker owns pending CALL records, abandoned correlations, PING output, HELLO and the socket writer.
stages.Bytes and messages: Active pending map has no application capacity. Abandoned unanswered count is capped at 256, with terminal transition on crossing. Heartbeat and one-shot open/kick metadata are different resources.
stages.Allocation: One pending entry per CALL, write Promise/catch continuations, payload clone references and control-message records.
stages.Copy count: Receiving the cloned view is not another explicit copy. Passing it to WriteQueue retains it until serialization/settlement.
stages.Backpressure: No count admission before pending insertion. Writes queue independently of map growth.
stages.Failure: Duplicate pending correlation fails closed. Write failure records terminal state. More than 256 processed abandons closes with 027.
stages.Cancellation: Abandon marks a record; it does not remove an unstarted wire CALL. A late reply retires the abandoned entry without delivering it.
stages.Ordering: CALL, EVENT and answer writes enter one writer. PING output must use the same authority.
stages.Fairness: No admission share between ordinary data and Worker-local control producers.
stages.Slow peer: Reading-but-never-replying peers permit unbounded active CALL state before caller timeouts. Healthy heartbeats do not prove application progress.
stages.Crash/restart cleanup: Worker end closes admission and arranges socket close; main has a five-second termination fallback after retained-ring drain. Credits must not be declared physically free just because STATE changed.
stages.Evidence: S05, S24; existing abandoned cap must remain distinct from proposed active-operation cap.

stages.Ownership: One WriteQueue per socket owns FIFO serialization and poison state. Promise closures retain caller payload references until their turn.
stages.Bytes and messages: No aggregate queue cap. Each payload is <=16 MiB. One active writer limits concurrent writes, not queued payloads.
stages.Allocation: Promise chain/catch records per frame. Active write allocates a 16-byte header and one complete contiguous envelope.
stages.Copy count: One full payload copy into the active envelope. Direct callers are not snapshotted at admission; a mutated queued payload changes later bytes.
stages.Backpressure: write returns a Promise; Worker does not await admission before taking more messages. DrainSignal wakes active write waits only.
stages.Failure: Oversize refusal emits no bytes and preserves the queue. A write-chain failure poisons later writes because the stream may contain a prefix.
stages.Cancellation: Caller timeout does not withdraw the closure or free retained payloads. A new bound must not release their credit at caller settlement.
stages.Ordering: Complete frames are serialized in enqueue order. This is a sound guard against byte interleaving.
stages.Fairness: Strict global FIFO; a large frame blocks all later frames. There is no per-channel scheduling guarantee.
stages.Slow peer: Zero progress reaches the five-second active deadline. A legal slow drain can keep servicing frames while the unbounded waiting tail grows.
stages.Crash/restart cleanup: Poison makes subsequent chain work fail rather than write. A terminal chain still contains existing callbacks until settlement/Worker teardown.
stages.Evidence: S02; 2,048 x 64 KiB payloads retained under an injected zero-progress writer, then all completed after release.

stages.Ownership: Bun Worker owns the client socket. Host owns the accepted server stream. OS owns kernel send/receive buffers and named-pipe I/O state.
stages.Bytes and messages: Kernel capacity is finite per endpoint but platform/configuration-dependent; no universal KELD process-wide total is declared. Stream buffers count bytes, not KIPC records.
stages.Allocation: Kernel buffers and any runtime staging are separate from JS/Rust owned payloads. UDS, diagnostic TCP and Windows named pipes need separate receipts.
stages.Copy count: User-to-kernel and kernel-to-user transfers must be reported separately. Source code alone does not establish physical memcpy count or zero-copy behavior.
stages.Backpressure: Bun raw write returns accepted bytes; partial/zero writes need drain handling. Host blocking writes stop their caller. No pressure reaches an unbounded upstream mailbox automatically.
stages.Failure: EOF, negative writes, OS timeout and partial-frame errors close/poison according to transport contract. Successful write proves local acceptance, not peer execution.
stages.Cancellation: Socket shutdown and reader polling are platform-sensitive. Retire only after real endpoint/worker completion.
stages.Ordering: One stream orders bytes. The writer must prevent interleaving at every shared use.
stages.Fairness: Kernel scheduling does not provide application channel fairness. Writer locks are not a fair queue contract.
stages.Slow peer: A no-read peer eventually blocks writes; a drip-reading peer tests absolute clocks, not only per-syscall timeouts.
stages.Crash/restart cleanup: Close descriptors/handles and revoke old generation before successor use. Do not treat flush or termination request as an acknowledgement.
stages.Evidence: S02, S15, S33, S35-S36. Actual probes in this audit used Unix sockets on macOS only.

stages.Ownership: keld-ipc link state machine and one generation-bound reader own the header/payload. Trusted context selects ReceivePolicy.
stages.Bytes and messages: One 16-byte header and one payload <=16 MiB per executing reader. Multiply by active/retiring readers; the reader cap is not a global process cap.
stages.Allocation: Payload Vec is allocated after length and semantic header validation. A new payload allocation occurs per frame.
stages.Copy count: Read fills the payload storage. Owned deserialization can add separate String/Vec storage later; that belongs to the decoder stage.
stages.Backpressure: Serial read/dispatch naturally stops reading during inline work or a blocking reply. Bounded worker admission may reject before decode.
stages.Failure: Malformed shape fails before payload allocation. A started frame has an absolute first-byte deadline. Idle polls intentionally do not time out a healthy quiet session.
stages.Cancellation: Short read polling checks stop/generation state. First-byte deadline cannot be renewed by fragments.
stages.Ordering: Wire frames read in stream order, with trusted generation validation before effects.
stages.Fairness: One reader per stream and sequential dispatch. No cross-channel fairness guarantee during a blocking handler/write.
stages.Slow peer: Trickled header/payload hits the absolute deadline, with documented poll or OS-timeout overshoot. No-reply application waits are separate.
stages.Crash/restart cleanup: Stale readers are made inert. Completed reader handles and stop registrations remain until session end today; D13 covers that metadata history.
stages.Evidence: S26, S20. Existing validation/deadline protections are preserved, not reported as missing.

stages.stage: 7. Decoder, schema and Rust handler admission
stages.Ownership: keld-ipc owns generic Postcard coding; schema owners own structural limits; Core owns FS/Auth scheduling; Native owns policy/effects.
stages.Bytes and messages: FS allows one outstanding native request with sync_channel(1). Auth has 32 tickets spanning queued/physical work and sync_channel(32). No common decoded-byte bound prices their graphs.
stages.Allocation: DeserializeOwned allocates nested Strings/Vecs. Wire frame and decoded graph coexist. encode uses to_allocvec; encode_into already exists for caller-owned storage.
stages.Copy count: Owned decoded strings/bytes generally copy from the wire. Rust FS output is encoded into another Vec; avoid assuming every schema has the same copy factor.
stages.Backpressure: FS/Auth bounded admission is useful and must be reused. Admission by record alone cannot price structural expansion.
stages.Failure: Guarded capacity refusal uses the existing IPC-owned CallError only under its documented consume-before-refuse conditions. Semantic policy rejection after decode does not undo allocation peaks.
stages.Cancellation: Native FS has a five-second cooperative operation budget. Auth tickets remain through physical drain. Transport timeout does not prove effect cancellation.
stages.Ordering: Per-owner scheduling and shared writer serialization apply. Existing request/effect order is part of the API contract.
stages.Fairness: Record caps are not byte fairness; many tiny decoded elements or a few maximum requests can dominate memory/work.
stages.Slow peer: Reply writers can retain decoded/output state while blocked. Answer capacity should be reserved before side effects when a reply is obligatory.
stages.Crash/restart cleanup: Generation retirement closes admission; retained physical work determines final release. No new parallel permission/parser owner should be added.
stages.Evidence: S16-S19; literal AuthRequest decode witness, not a Native auth acceptance result.

stages.stage: 8. Host dispatcher, UI commands and physical consumer
stages.Ownership: Core WindowSession/registry owns request admission. mpsc, wake bridge and Tao own successive handoffs. The native UI loop owns effects.
stages.Bytes and messages: Unbounded command mpsc and no credit carried through Tao. 1,024 window identities and 64 pending Destroy records per window are separate bounds.
stages.Allocation: Queue nodes, command records and any referenced objects. Payload ownership can move while total retained command count remains unchanged.
stages.Copy count: Rust commands move through channels/proxy. Moves are not proof of allocation-free queues; runtime/event nodes still exist.
stages.Backpressure: send_window_setter enqueues and replies Accepted without waiting for UI consumption. Producer may await every reply and still overrun the UI.
stages.Failure: Disconnected queue is an error. Capacity exhaustion has no current defined result. A correction must refuse before enqueue/Accepted.
stages.Cancellation: Physical teardown and generation checks exist. A bounded permit must survive forwarding and release only at a proven terminal consumer boundary.
stages.Ordering: Command enqueue order and native dispatch order must remain consistent. Do not silently coalesce effectful requests.
stages.Fairness: Repeated setters on one window can occupy all backlog. Reserve terminal/control capacity without letting ordinary commands consume it.
stages.Slow peer: A stalled UI accumulates commands even with a fast socket. A slow socket also blocks shared writer/transition owners.
stages.Crash/restart cleanup: Carry generation-tagged permits through the bridge; stale work must not free successor capacity. Avoid a blocking bounded send while holding shutdown locks.
stages.Evidence: S11-S13, S25, S30; 4,096 retained Accepted setters on one live window.

stages.Ownership: Native window observer produces state facts. Core event coordinator filters and writes them back to the role.
stages.Bytes and messages: Unbounded mpsc before changed-only filtering. Four facts can be emitted for one state observation.
stages.Allocation: One retained queue entry per emitted fact, plus implementation-dependent node/block overhead. Registry/filter state is a different retained domain.
stages.Copy count: Owned fixed-size facts move through the queue and encode to output; exact allocator/node costs require measurement.
stages.Backpressure: UI sends do not wait for coordinator or role consumption. Synchronous writer can stop the coordinator.
stages.Failure: Current channel disconnect handling does not define overload. A new bounded mailbox needs explicit terminal behavior for lossless facts.
stages.Cancellation: Lifecycle/terminal events need reserved capacity and a nonblocking UI-facing path. Drop-oldest is not a cancellation protocol.
stages.Ordering: Created/Close/Released and state events may have observable order. Deduplicating after queueing is not an admission mechanism.
stages.Fairness: State floods can starve lifecycle delivery unless admission/scheduling rules protect it.
stages.Slow peer: A role that drains more slowly than native observations are produced can grow this queue indefinitely while each individual write still succeeds.
stages.Crash/restart cleanup: Retired-generation facts must be rejected/retired by the canonical owner. Bounded bridge state must not survive indefinitely into successors.
stages.Evidence: S11, S14, S25, S30. Source finding; no AppKit flood run was claimed.

stages.stage: 10. Bun FrameReader, shared ring and blocking reply slot
stages.Ownership: Worker FrameReader owns socket fragments/fill. Worker is sole ring writer; main applies and dispatches using atomic indices. One separate slot carries the blocking reply.
stages.Bytes and messages: Default SAB=64+65,536+1,048,576=1,114,176 bytes. Ring <=16,384 records and available bytes. FrameReader unread bytes <=one frame envelope after checks and <=65,536 fragments. Allocated backing is larger than received-byte count.
stages.Allocation: Owned callback chunks, active full-size fill, copied payload, fixed SAB and main ringCopy allocations. Callback is copied before aggregate rejection; peak requires a qualified callback-size allowance.
stages.Copy count: Contiguous input: callback copy, gather payload, ring copy, main delivery copy. Fragmented fill copies later fragments directly; state appliers can add a separate copy, and generated response decoding another.
stages.Backpressure: Ring overflow closes with 026; v2 has no live GRANT credit. The ring is a fail-closed bound, not elastic buffering for unlimited producers.
stages.Failure: Overflow retains earlier records for ordered drain. Blocking reply larger than its slot also fails. Default async ring cannot hold the valid large FS result in D09.
stages.Cancellation: Caller deadline drains retained replies before deciding abandon. Closing drains earlier retained facts before source end; that correct ordering must remain.
stages.Ordering: One atomic ring plus reply position, first-terminal-wins state and coalesced KICK preserve the current contract. Separate ring lanes would need a new ordering proof.
stages.Fairness: Dispatch processes a finite snapshot of W_BYTES, but arbitrary listener duration is unbounded. Count/byte limits do not imply a scheduling-time bound.
stages.Slow peer: A parked main can fill the ring; overflow is terminal, not drop/coalesce. A slow async handler may leave the ring empty while retaining work elsewhere.
stages.Crash/restart cleanup: Worker liveness while parked, terminal notification, ordered drain and eventual terminate exist. One end notification or a zero counter is not a physical reclamation proof.
stages.Evidence: S04 S06 S24 S29; preserve existing guards and differentiate their actual scope.

stages.Ownership: WorkerLink owns listeners, state appliers and host-CALL continuations. Application owns its own listener registrations, result retention and arbitrary internal allocations.
stages.Bytes and messages: No transport handler-concurrency cap. Event listener registrations are application-managed and unbounded by this transport. Application-retained results are outside transport-owned byte bounds.
stages.Allocation: ringCopy creates an independent payload. CALL Promise.then retains handler lifecycle state. Finalization copies pending values into an array before clearing, adding a proportional peak.
stages.Copy count: One delivery copy; state applier can separately copy the same EVENT. Response decoders may allocate independent content. Do not sum aliases as distinct backing stores.
stages.Backpressure: Synchronous event callback delays ring release. An async listener return is not awaited. CALL ring release precedes asynchronous handler completion.
stages.Failure: Thrown event listener errors are isolated/deferred. Handler throws/rejections end the link. Valid late handler answers after terminal state are suppressed.
stages.Cancellation: No automatic AbortSignal for application code. Bounded admission is enforceable; forced completion of arbitrary JS within the role requires process isolation/termination.
stages.Ordering: Dispatch order is FIFO. Async completion order can differ. Replies must correlate independently; do not promise completion order merely from input order.
stages.Fairness: A long synchronous callback can monopolize the role main thread. A scheduling slice cannot preempt arbitrary user code.
stages.Slow peer: Many handlers can stay unresolved after the ring drains, as the 512-handler probe demonstrated.
stages.Crash/restart cleanup: Transport can seal admission and suppress stale replies. It cannot reclaim objects that live application code still owns; a successor uses fresh generation identity.
stages.Evidence: S04; exact close behavior observed in the handler barrier experiment.

stages.Ownership: Core and Runtime own generation fencing, reader stop flags, JoinHandles, child cleanup and successor admission.
stages.Bytes and messages: Reader handle map and stop-flag vector grow across completed generations until final session stop. Sliding-window crash suppression is not a lifetime resource cap.
stages.Allocation: Per-generation reader state, JoinHandle/result packets, Arc flags, map/vector capacity and per-link fixed buffers while generations overlap.
stages.Copy count: Mostly metadata ownership; count retained entries and capacities rather than assuming all stopped threads remain live.
stages.Backpressure: There is no bounded completed-reader reaper today. New generation work can continue while historical records remain retained.
stages.Failure: Terminal join observes thread failures. Removing historical entries too early can lose failure evidence or race stale callbacks.
stages.Cancellation: Do not synchronously join on the guardian owner whose acknowledgement a reader awaits. Completion/reaping must occur outside that dependency cycle.
stages.Ordering: Retire old authority before enabling successor. Ticket epoch and slot incarnation prevent old release from altering new capacity.
stages.Fairness: Reaping needs bounded scheduled progress so a long-lived session does not accumulate history.
stages.Slow peer: A retirement that cannot finish needs a finite overlapping-generation budget and terminal escalation; simply allocating another ledger compounds memory.
stages.Crash/restart cleanup: Observe actual Worker/thread/process exit, socket closure and record removal separately. A close request is not cleanup completion.
stages.Evidence: S20; app_session.rs:2360-2367 and 8050-8060; source finding, no restart-soak measurement.

tests.name: EVENT byte budget
tests.positive: Pause a real authenticated peer after HELLO. Keep record capacity ample. Flood uniquely marked 64 KiB/1 MiB/max-size payloads past B_data. Independent retained-buffer census must remain <=B_data; refused operations emit zero bytes.
tests.mutant: Remove only pre-post EVENT byte reservation. The independent census exceeds B_data before active-write timeout.
tests.status: Current defect witnessed; bounded implementation/mutant pair not run.

tests.name: Message count independent of bytes
tests.positive: Use zero-length or minimum-size legal EVENTs and ample byte budget. Admit exactly N_data, then try one more.
tests.mutant: Remove only record admission. N_data+1 live envelopes are retained even though bytes fit.
tests.status: Specified.

tests.name: Concurrent producer arbitration
tests.positive: Use32 logical producers for acceptance/FIFO load. For the atomicity mutant, barrier a real main-thread reservation against a Worker credit return on the same shared bytes-used counter; both read the old value before either updates. Check counter against independent live tickets, then attempt capacity-filling admissions.
tests.mutant: Replace only the shared atomic read-modify-write with a load/store pair. Main reservation and Worker release lose an update; independent live tickets disagree with credit and later admission exceeds capacity. A separate single-fault rollback arm leaks partially reserved credit.
tests.status: Specified; logical Promise concurrency alone cannot falsify synchronous admission atomicity. The negative arm requires the actual two-agent shared-counter schedule.

tests.name: Backing stores and immutable ordinary input
tests.positive: Post a one-byte view into an 8 MiB backing and a pooled-buffer slice. Hold the writer, mutate caller storage, then compare admitted and peer digests plus actual backing sizes. Test direct WriteQueue separately so a mailbox clone cannot hide aliasing.
tests.mutant: Post the original view or omit the direct snapshot. Backing census exceeds charge or peer bytes differ.
tests.status: Both baseline alias/backing witnesses executed.

tests.name: Shared-backed input
tests.positive: Supply an SAB-backed view and mutate it from another agent while the boundary is paused. Contract must either reject before dispatch or use a separately proved synchronization protocol.
tests.mutant: Remove shared-backing rejection while retaining ordinary copy behavior. Shared input reaches the unsynchronized path. Do not accept a potentially torn memcpy as a positive snapshot oracle.
tests.status: Shared alias probe executed; future rejection test specified.

tests.name: Pre-Ready and encoder limits
tests.positive: Complete HELLO but withhold Ready. Offer enough valid FS/auth calls to fill operation and encoder budgets. Observe reservations before UTF-8/vector/snapshot allocation.
tests.mutant: Move admission to WorkerLink only. Pre-Ready encoded payload or waiter census exceeds its bound. Separately remove bounded encoder preflight; over-limit allocation occurs before refusal.
tests.status: Encoder baseline executed; pre-Ready source finding.

tests.name: Active CALL records
tests.positive: Peer drains requests promptly but returns no replies. Long valid deadlines keep abandoned count zero. Byte budget stays mostly free.
tests.mutant: Release CALL records when writes complete. Main/Worker pending count exceeds N_call although queued payload bytes remain low.
tests.status: Specified.

tests.name: Timeout does not free retained bytes
tests.positive: Hold a queued/partial frame, expire its caller, then use the apparently free capacity for other work. Observe live buffers independently.
tests.mutant: Release byte credit on caller timeout. Live retained bytes exceed B_out.
tests.status: Specified; source confirms timeout does not remove current writer work.

tests.name: Permanent tombstone saturation
tests.positive: Use N_call128 below256; occupy other partitions while retaining prepaid abandon rights and the reserved terminal right. Expire all calls, keep peer alive and never answer. No new CALL is submitted and no abandon acquires a fresh control slot.
tests.mutant: Disable the permanent-saturation terminal transition, keeping local refusals. Link stays OPEN and unable to admit past the promised retirement deadline.
tests.status: Specified; existing PR1413 AC14 owns this interaction.

tests.name: Late reply vs retirement
tests.positive: Deliver the exact old reply immediately before and after terminal commitment in separate barrier schedules. Check caller result, tombstone count and next operation.
tests.mutant: Drop the tombstone/reuse the correlation early. Old reply settles the wrong call or capacity is released twice.
tests.status: Specified.

tests.name: Handler concurrency
tests.positive: Override the common profile: N_handler=1, at least2 answer ticket slots, and B_answer>=2*c_max (6F if c_max=3F); raise B_out and N_out equally. Hold one handler and submit a second valid CALL, pacing input to avoid ring saturation. Reserve2F of handler-input storage independently so that gate also stays open.
tests.mutant: Remove only handler-record reservation. Active handler count exceeds N_handler. A ring overflow must not mask this mutation.

blocks.text: 1. Verdict and scope

KIPC does not currently provide an end-to-end bounded resource contract. Several local limits work, but ownership moves into unbounded mailboxes, Promise chains, handler continuations and Host UI queues. A maximum frame length and a bounded shared inbound ring do not bound the full pipeline. The smallest correction is composed admission and lifetime accounting inside the existing owners, with a permit held until the actual consumer retires the work.

Baseline: published main 269d51528137faf574cfd3548586ee3ada1acfda, retrieved 23 November 2026. Existing GH623 proposal: PR1413 at 870d1c693214e5b20bc8cdc900afa3ded67e2823. The PR is open and not merged; its file remains Status:draft. B1 capacity/copy selection, B2 local failure semantics and B3 platform qualification remain open. This audit extends that existing work instead of inventing another transport or tracker. [S31-S32]

Scope covers the canonical app-link transport, generated FS/auth/echo consumers, production Core dispatch, macOS UI handoffs, decoder ownership and generation cleanup. Destination-only GRANT, remote cancellation, general schema generation and optional bulk transport are not credited as current protections. Native execution here is macOS only; this is not Windows/Linux acceptance or a full application qualification.

No production implementation, branch, PR, issue or review was changed. Rust witnesses add44 test lines only in an isolated source archive. TypeScript probes import the pinned production code. The files are reproduction tools and design evidence, not proof that a new bound has been implemented.

rows: Census and copies

Existing resource owner: any clone, pending record, queue insertion or handler effect before its reservation falsifies admission.

blocks.text: The first WorkerLink test invocation had four subprocess launch failures because bare bun was missing from PATH. The explicit-path/PATH rerun passed10/10; the initial output is preserved. One initial Rust filter selected zero tests and is not used as evidence. The corrected resource_audit_ command ran both Rust witnesses. Full workspace tests, native installed-product qualification and the future ledger mutation suite were not run.
3. Ranked defect ledger

P1 means this defect prevents a credible boundedness or compatibility claim and should block acceptance of that claim. P2 means a separate lifetime/liveness/fairness correction is required. These ranks are not invented CVSS scores. Executed witnesses and source-only findings are explicitly separated.
D01 | P1 | Outbound mailbox and writer retention

Evidence class: Executed + source. WorkerLink posts without admission; WriteQueue retains payload closures without byte or message caps. A no-read synthetic peer accepted 512 x 64 KiB. An injected stalled writer retained 2,048 payloads / 128 MiB. The active-write timeout begins at service, so it cannot cap producer bursts or queue age. [S02 S03 S05]
Minimal correction: One ledger before the first retention; finite bytes, records and residence time; no admission waiters.
D02 | P1 | Pre-Ready work escapes a Worker-only limit

Evidence class: Source + encoder probe. FS encodes before its first await; invokeFs/invokeAuth then await whenReady. Each whenReady can add a promise/waiter. A healthy link that never sends Ready can retain any number of encoded requests. Moving admission only into WorkerLink leaves this path untouched. [S07 S08 S09 S10]
Minimal correction: Reserve at the public adapter before encoding or readiness retention. Preserve direct whenReady semantics; refuse excess operation records locally.
D03 | P1 | Active CALL state has no aggregate bound

Evidence class: Source. Main creates a timer, Promise and Map record per call. Worker creates its own pending record. The 256-abandoned cap acts only after timeouts are processed; it does not bound active calls or a burst before that point. A peer can drain writes and withhold replies while byte use stays low. [S03 S05]
Minimal correction: Keep one operation record until caller settlement AND Worker pending/tombstone retirement AND terminal delivery. Bound tombstone retirement separately.
D04 | P1 | Inbound ring drains into unbounded handlers

Evidence class: Executed + source. The ring releases a CALL before startCallHandler. A real socket probe with eight ring slots started 512 unresolved handlers. After close, all 512 continuations resumed when their barrier opened; late answers were suppressed. Closing a transport does not cancel arbitrary application promises. [S04]
Minimal correction: Reserve handler count, input retention and maximum answer bytes before invoking application code; prevent further invocation on exhaustion.
D05 | P1 | Host acknowledges an unbounded UI backlog

Evidence class: Executed component + source. One window produced 4,096 Accepted replies while 4,096 setter commands remained unconsumed. The registry window/destroy limits are different resources. The wake bridge forwards into Tao, so bounding only the mpsc channel would move retention downstream. [S11 S12 S13 S25]
Minimal correction: Reserve before enqueue and before Accepted. Transfer the same permit through Tao; release on physical UI consumption or proven discard.
D06 | P1 | Native facts accumulate before filtering

Evidence class: Source. UI observations enqueue four state facts through unbounded mpsc. Changed-only filtering occurs later in Core. The coordinator can wait on the shared writer while native observations continue. Duplicate filtering after the queue cannot bound that queue. [S11 S14 S25 S30]
Minimal correction: A bounded native-to-Core mailbox with reserved lifecycle capacity. UI must not block. Coalescing requires explicit state-event semantics.
D07 | P1 | Backing storage and shared-input ownership are unpriced

Evidence class: Executed runtime + source. A one-byte Uint8Array view cloned an 8 MiB backing buffer on Bun 1.4.4. SharedArrayBuffer stayed shared and a post-send mutation was visible to the receiver. Direct WriteQueue also sent a later mutation. The low-level immutable-snapshot promise is currently unclear; the alias is demonstrated, not an invented existing API guarantee. [S02 S03 S28]

Minimal correction: Compact ordinary input after admission; charge copy overlap. Reject shared-backed input or specify a synchronization protocol. Copying an unsynchronized SAB is not a coherent snapshot proof.
D08 | P1 | Codec and reader allocation differ from wire bytes

Evidence class: Executed + source. 262,151 AuthRequest wire bytes decoded into 262,144 empty strings; vector capacity alone was 8,388,480 bytes. The 32-call auth limit is a record bound. FS encoded an over-limit string before rejecting it. FrameReader accounts received fill bytes rather than the allocated fill capacity and copies callbacks before its aggregate check. These are amplification/transient proof gaps, not infinite single-frame allocation claims. [S06 S07 S16 S17 S18 S27]
Minimal correction: Schema-owned cardinality and decoded-storage limits before allocation; bounded encoder scratch; separately price callback, active fill, owned chunks and decode overlap.
D09 | P1 | Legal FS result cannot fit the default async ring

Evidence class: Executed transport + source. Native FS permits 8 MiB. Default WorkerLink ring is 1 MiB. An independently encoded valid response for a 2 MiB file had a 2,097,173-byte envelope and failed with KELD-IPC-026 in an otherwise empty default ring. The probe exercised real WorkerLink/UDS, not a real filesystem Host call. [S07 S19 S24 S29]

Minimal correction: For the API role, provision a ring large enough for its largest legal encoded response, counted globally. With power-of-two rings, an 8 MiB result needs a 16 MiB ring. An alternate reply lane is a larger design.
D10 | P1 | Rust active write lacks an absolute frame clock

Evidence class: Source + official contract. write_frame uses write_all(header), write_all(payload), then flush. OS write timeouts constrain individual waits. Repeated successful short writes can outlast the intended frame budget while shared generation/transition locks remain held. A no-read peer does time out. A finite frame is not claimed to make positive progress literally forever. [S15 S30 S35 S36]
Minimal correction: One absolute header+payload+flush deadline; remaining-time waits; poison after a partial failure. Cancellation/close must not need the lock held by blocked I/O.
D11 | P2 | Queue residence and control fairness have no bound

Evidence class: Source. The writer is FIFO and its five-second clock starts only when a frame becomes active. Control, answers, abandon and close can sit behind admitted data. Reserved admission credit cannot make them overtake existing FIFO work. Strict ordering supplies no independent per-channel latency guarantee. [S02 S05 S28]
Minimal correction: Preserve FIFO. Add admission-to-service and close deadlines plus bounded admission shares. Do not add a priority queue that changes accepted order.
D12 | P2 | One renderer response can wait without end

Evidence class: Source. The renderer bridge repeats recv_timeout(APP_LINK_READER_POLL) until reply, disconnect or stop. There is no overall response deadline. One pending slot bounds memory but can hold the renderer dispatcher indefinitely while a live Bun handler never answers. [S21]
Minimal correction: Give the caller an absolute response deadline and bounded late-reply ownership; do not replay an unknown effect.
D13 | P2 | Retired reader metadata grows with session history

Evidence class: Source. Each generation appends a stop Arc and retains its JoinHandle. Retirement defers joins to terminal shutdown to avoid a real guardian acknowledgement deadlock. Spaced restarts can outlive the sliding crash window and grow retained history. This is metadata/result retention, not demonstrated live-thread leakage. [S20 S37 S38 S39]
Minimal correction: Reap completed retired readers asynchronously outside the dependency cycle. Bound the reaper backlog and stop registrations before admitting more generations.
D14 | P1 contract | Architecture text can permit unsafe reasoning

Evidence class: Source contradiction. Architecture02 equates pending post-Quit 022 with 024, while approved GH527 says 022 means effect unknown and only host 024 proves nonexecution. It also presents remote cancellation and allocation-free calls without accurate Current/Target status. Live timeout merely abandons correlation; it does not cancel queued or remote work. [S01 S03 S05 S23]
Minimal correction: Correct the exact architecture text, retain typed failure distinctions, and prohibit automatic replay of unanswered calls.
4. Complete stage inventory

The following inventory follows Producer -> postMessage -> Worker -> WriteQueue -> socket -> Host reader -> decoder -> dispatcher -> consumer, then the reverse path and retirement. Each stage states all requested properties. A missing configured capacity is explicitly called unbounded; a known finite amplification is not mislabeled as infinite.
1. Public producer, generated encoder and readiness

rows: Ownership
Application owns inputs until the adapter snapshots them. Generated FS/auth codecs own serialized payloads. app.ts owns Ready waiters and the singleton link attempt.
Bytes and messages
No aggregate pre-Ready operation/byte cap. Frame limit is 16 MiB after several encoders have allocated. Direct whenReady waiters have no count bound.
Allocation
String UTF-8 buffers, byte snapshots, joined payload, Promise continuations and per-call Ready waiters. Auth vectors create per-element objects/arrays.
Copy count
FS Write normally copies content into encodeBytes, then into joinPayload: two source-visible content copies before posting. UTF-8 encoding is a representation allocation, counted separately.
Backpressure
No feedback from socket or UI consumption reaches this retained pre-Ready work. A singleton connection attempt does not bound its subscribers.
Failure
Local codec errors reject async APIs. Link failure rejects readiness waiters. An authenticated but never-Ready link is a distinct indefinite wait.
Cancellation
No public operation cancellation here. Waiting time before transport call is outside its later call deadline.
Ordering
Snapshot occurs before readiness yields. FIFO guarantees begin at post order, not arbitrary concurrent API invocation order.
Fairness
No producer quota or bounded admission arbitration. Application scheduling determines call order.
Slow peer
Withheld Ready retains requests without requiring a blocked socket. High-rate producers can grow this graph indefinitely.
Crash/restart cleanup
A failed singleton is not reset for reconnect. Failure rejects waiters, but only actual reference retirement and GC reclaim objects.
Evidence
S07-S10, S27; executed oversized-string allocation probe.

blocks.text: 2. Main-to-Worker postMessage boundary

rows: Ownership
WorkerLink owns a private MessagePort; Bun owns serialized/in-transit message storage. One FIFO carries data and control.
Bytes and messages
No configured cap. sendEvent posts after per-frame validation. CALLs add main pending state before posting.
Allocation
Message envelope, runtime clone storage, and closure/control metadata. A tiny view can clone a much larger backing store.
Copy count
Ordinary ArrayBuffer input is cloned at this boundary in the executed Bun probe. Exact transient overlap/native storage is not proven. Shared backing aliases rather than snapshots.
Backpressure
postMessage returns void. It does not wait for Worker service or socket drain.
Failure
Synchronous clone/post failure must roll back every reservation and pending record in the future design. Current code has no aggregate capacity failure.
Cancellation
Abandon and close are messages behind earlier posts; they do not remove messages already posted.
Ordering
The captured native port method preserves the existing single outbound FIFO. A second independent queue would create another ordering owner.
Fairness
Data can consume all available runtime queue storage before terminal metadata is serviced. FIFO alone gives no channel share.
Slow peer
Worker can drain the port faster than the socket by moving work into WriteQueue. Neither local queue is bounded.
Crash/restart cleanup
Terminal STATE stops new public work; Worker exit/termination handles transport lifetime. Physical mailbox reclamation must be qualified independently.
Evidence
S03, S05, S28, S34; native UDS flood and backing-store probes.

blocks.text: 3. Worker operation records and local producers

rows: Ownership
TransportWorker owns pending CALL records, abandoned correlations, PING output, HELLO and the socket writer.
Bytes and messages
Active pending map has no application capacity. Abandoned unanswered count is capped at 256, with terminal transition on crossing. Heartbeat and one-shot open/kick metadata are different resources.
Allocation
One pending entry per CALL, write Promise/catch continuations, payload clone references and control-message records.
Copy count
Receiving the cloned view is not another explicit copy. Passing it to WriteQueue retains it until serialization/settlement.
Backpressure
No count admission before pending insertion. Writes queue independently of map growth.
Failure
Duplicate pending correlation fails closed. Write failure records terminal state. More than 256 processed abandons closes with 027.
Cancellation
Abandon marks a record; it does not remove an unstarted wire CALL. A late reply retires the abandoned entry without delivering it.
Ordering
CALL, EVENT and answer writes enter one writer. PING output must use the same authority.
Fairness
No admission share between ordinary data and Worker-local control producers.
Slow peer
Reading-but-never-replying peers permit unbounded active CALL state before caller timeouts. Healthy heartbeats do not prove application progress.
Crash/restart cleanup
Worker end closes admission and arranges socket close; main has a five-second termination fallback after retained-ring drain. Credits must not be declared physically free just because STATE changed.
Evidence
S05, S24; existing abandoned cap must remain distinct from proposed active-operation cap.

blocks.text: 4. WriteQueue and active frame serialization

rows: Ownership
One WriteQueue per socket owns FIFO serialization and poison state. Promise closures retain caller payload references until their turn.
Bytes and messages
No aggregate queue cap. Each payload is <=16 MiB. One active writer limits concurrent writes, not queued payloads.
Allocation
Promise chain/catch records per frame. Active write allocates a 16-byte header and one complete contiguous envelope.
Copy count
One full payload copy into the active envelope. Direct callers are not snapshotted at admission; a mutated queued payload changes later bytes.
Backpressure
write returns a Promise; Worker does not await admission before taking more messages. DrainSignal wakes active write waits only.
Failure
Oversize refusal emits no bytes and preserves the queue. A write-chain failure poisons later writes because the stream may contain a prefix.
Cancellation
Caller timeout does not withdraw the closure or free retained payloads. A new bound must not release their credit at caller settlement.
Ordering
Complete frames are serialized in enqueue order. This is a sound guard against byte interleaving.
Fairness
Strict global FIFO; a large frame blocks all later frames. There is no per-channel scheduling guarantee.
Slow peer
Zero progress reaches the five-second active deadline. A legal slow drain can keep servicing frames while the unbounded waiting tail grows.
Crash/restart cleanup
Poison makes subsequent chain work fail rather than write. A terminal chain still contains existing callbacks until settlement/Worker teardown.
Evidence
S02; 2,048 x 64 KiB payloads retained under an injected zero-progress writer, then all completed after release.

blocks.text: 5. Socket and OS buffers

rows: Ownership
Bun Worker owns the client socket. Host owns the accepted server stream. OS owns kernel send/receive buffers and named-pipe I/O state.
Bytes and messages
Kernel capacity is finite per endpoint but platform/configuration-dependent; no universal KELD process-wide total is declared. Stream buffers count bytes, not KIPC records.
Allocation
Kernel buffers and any runtime staging are separate from JS/Rust owned payloads. UDS, diagnostic TCP and Windows named pipes need separate receipts.
Copy count
User-to-kernel and kernel-to-user transfers must be reported separately. Source code alone does not establish physical memcpy count or zero-copy behavior.
Backpressure
Bun raw write returns accepted bytes; partial/zero writes need drain handling. Host blocking writes stop their caller. No pressure reaches an unbounded upstream mailbox automatically.
Failure
EOF, negative writes, OS timeout and partial-frame errors close/poison according to transport contract. Successful write proves local acceptance, not peer execution.
Cancellation
Socket shutdown and reader polling are platform-sensitive. Retire only after real endpoint/worker completion.
Ordering
One stream orders bytes. The writer must prevent interleaving at every shared use.
Fairness
Kernel scheduling does not provide application channel fairness. Writer locks are not a fair queue contract.
Slow peer
A no-read peer eventually blocks writes; a drip-reading peer tests absolute clocks, not only per-syscall timeouts.
Crash/restart cleanup
Close descriptors/handles and revoke old generation before successor use. Do not treat flush or termination request as an acknowledgement.
Evidence
S02, S15, S33, S35-S36. Actual probes in this audit used Unix sockets on macOS only.

blocks.text: 6. Rust host reader and validation

rows: Ownership
keld-ipc link state machine and one generation-bound reader own the header/payload. Trusted context selects ReceivePolicy.
Bytes and messages
One 16-byte header and one payload <=16 MiB per executing reader. Multiply by active/retiring readers; the reader cap is not a global process cap.
Allocation
Payload Vec is allocated after length and semantic header validation. A new payload allocation occurs per frame.
Copy count
Read fills the payload storage. Owned deserialization can add separate String/Vec storage later; that belongs to the decoder stage.
Backpressure
Serial read/dispatch naturally stops reading during inline work or a blocking reply. Bounded worker admission may reject before decode.
Failure
Malformed shape fails before payload allocation. A started frame has an absolute first-byte deadline. Idle polls intentionally do not time out a healthy quiet session.
Cancellation
Short read polling checks stop/generation state. First-byte deadline cannot be renewed by fragments.
Ordering
Wire frames read in stream order, with trusted generation validation before effects.
Fairness
One reader per stream and sequential dispatch. No cross-channel fairness guarantee during a blocking handler/write.
Slow peer
Trickled header/payload hits the absolute deadline, with documented poll or OS-timeout overshoot. No-reply application waits are separate.
Crash/restart cleanup
Stale readers are made inert. Completed reader handles and stop registrations remain until session end today; D13 covers that metadata history.
Evidence
S26, S20. Existing validation/deadline protections are preserved, not reported as missing.

blocks.text: 7. Decoder, schema and Rust handler admission

rows: Ownership
keld-ipc owns generic Postcard coding; schema owners own structural limits; Core owns FS/Auth scheduling; Native owns policy/effects.
Bytes and messages
FS allows one outstanding native request with sync_channel(1). Auth has 32 tickets spanning queued/physical work and sync_channel(32). No common decoded-byte bound prices their graphs.
Allocation
DeserializeOwned allocates nested Strings/Vecs. Wire frame and decoded graph coexist. encode uses to_allocvec; encode_into already exists for caller-owned storage.
Copy count
Owned decoded strings/bytes generally copy from the wire. Rust FS output is encoded into another Vec; avoid assuming every schema has the same copy factor.
Backpressure
FS/Auth bounded admission is useful and must be reused. Admission by record alone cannot price structural expansion.
Failure
Guarded capacity refusal uses the existing IPC-owned CallError only under its documented consume-before-refuse conditions. Semantic policy rejection after decode does not undo allocation peaks.
Cancellation
Native FS has a five-second cooperative operation budget. Auth tickets remain through physical drain. Transport timeout does not prove effect cancellation.
Ordering
Per-owner scheduling and shared writer serialization apply. Existing request/effect order is part of the API contract.
Fairness
Record caps are not byte fairness; many tiny decoded elements or a few maximum requests can dominate memory/work.
Slow peer
Reply writers can retain decoded/output state while blocked. Answer capacity should be reserved before side effects when a reply is obligatory.
Crash/restart cleanup
Generation retirement closes admission; retained physical work determines final release. No new parallel permission/parser owner should be added.
Evidence
S16-S19; literal AuthRequest decode witness, not a Native auth acceptance result.

blocks.text: 8. Host dispatcher, UI commands and physical consumer

rows: Ownership
Core WindowSession/registry owns request admission. mpsc, wake bridge and Tao own successive handoffs. The native UI loop owns effects.
Bytes and messages
Unbounded command mpsc and no credit carried through Tao. 1,024 window identities and 64 pending Destroy records per window are separate bounds.
Allocation
Queue nodes, command records and any referenced objects. Payload ownership can move while total retained command count remains unchanged.
Copy count
Rust commands move through channels/proxy. Moves are not proof of allocation-free queues; runtime/event nodes still exist.
Backpressure
send_window_setter enqueues and replies Accepted without waiting for UI consumption. Producer may await every reply and still overrun the UI.
Failure
Disconnected queue is an error. Capacity exhaustion has no current defined result. A correction must refuse before enqueue/Accepted.
Cancellation
Physical teardown and generation checks exist. A bounded permit must survive forwarding and release only at a proven terminal consumer boundary.
Ordering
Command enqueue order and native dispatch order must remain consistent. Do not silently coalesce effectful requests.
Fairness
Repeated setters on one window can occupy all backlog. Reserve terminal/control capacity without letting ordinary commands consume it.
Slow peer
A stalled UI accumulates commands even with a fast socket. A slow socket also blocks shared writer/transition owners.
Crash/restart cleanup
Carry generation-tagged permits through the bridge; stale work must not free successor capacity. Avoid a blocking bounded send while holding shutdown locks.
Evidence
S11-S13, S25, S30; 4,096 retained Accepted setters on one live window.

blocks.text: 9. Native event return path

rows: Ownership
Native window observer produces state facts. Core event coordinator filters and writes them back to the role.
Bytes and messages
Unbounded mpsc before changed-only filtering. Four facts can be emitted for one state observation.
Allocation
One retained queue entry per emitted fact, plus implementation-dependent node/block overhead. Registry/filter state is a different retained domain.
Copy count
Owned fixed-size facts move through the queue and encode to output; exact allocator/node costs require measurement.
Backpressure
UI sends do not wait for coordinator or role consumption. Synchronous writer can stop the coordinator.

blocks.text: 5. Queueing and resource model

Let A_i(t) be admitted records at stage i, D_i(t) records retired at the actual consumer, Q_i(t) retained records, and B_i(t) retained backing bytes. Count allocations by backing identity and capacity, not merely each view length. Count payload-free records separately.

Q_i(t) = Q_i(0) + A_i(t) - D_i(t)
B_i(t) = sum(capacity of distinct live backing allocations owned by stage i)
If admitted byte rate a_i > retirement byte rate d_i for an unbounded interval,
B_i grows with the integral of (a_i - d_i), unless admission stops or the owner ends.
A per-frame maximum M gives payload_bytes <= M * Q_i only when Q_i is bounded.

The queueing failure is compositional. A worker can drain its mailbox into an unbounded writer, keeping mailbox occupancy low. The main thread can drain a bounded ring into unresolved handlers. Core can acknowledge setters while native commands remain queued. None of those local observations proves that the system consumed the work.

Five-second active I/O timeouts do not create a universal byte cap. An arbitrarily large finite burst can allocate before that timeout runs. Under sustained slow-but-progressing service, each frame can finish within its own budget while the waiting tail grows indefinitely. Finite call deadlines only bound lifetime at a fixed producer rate, and the rate is not an enforced contract. Little's law, L=lambda*W, is a useful steady-state cross-check, not a hard admission bound.

For each live ticket j:
  reserve worst_case_simultaneous_backing(j) before retention
  sum(charge_bytes(j)) <= B_out
  live_ticket_count <= N_out
  distinct CALL tickets in pending/tombstone/completion states <= N_call
  active_handler_count <= N_handler
  UI_commands_not_physically_retired <= N_ui
  native_facts_not_retired <= N_events
  retired_readers_not_reaped <= N_retired
  admission_waiter_count = 0

A ticket may release payload bytes before it releases its CALL record. A successful request write does not retire the waiting call. A timeout settles the caller but does not retire an unreceived request, Worker tombstone or running handler. A slot reused by a new generation requires both ledger epoch and slot incarnation. A zero logical counter does not prove that Bun has reclaimed an old mailbox or that an OS process has exited.

M_owned_live <= B_out + B_inbound + B_decode + B_encoder_scratch
               + B_UI_commands + B_native_facts + B_generation_metadata
               + B_bounded_completion_records

M_process additionally includes runtime/GC/allocator capacity, native buffers,
application-owned retention. Kernel socket/pipe storage is separate and is not process RSS. A complete resource census counts both domains; a hard RSS claim needs
explicit bounds for those terms and for live + retiring generations. None is inferred here.

The current shared inbound allocation is exactly64 + replyBytes + ringBytes. At defaults it is1,114,176 bytes. Usable ring records are no more than min(ringRecords, floor(ringBytes/16)); schemas can impose a larger minimum record size. FrameReader received-byte accounting is not allocated-capacity accounting: a one-byte partial payload can already own the entire declared fill. Include active fill, queued chunks, callback storage, copy overlap and metadata separately. [S06 S24]

An8MiB content result needs more than8MiB after Postcard/header overhead, so the present power-of-two configuration needs16MiB for this API profile. That choice is correctness accommodation, not an optimization claim. Multiply the larger fixed allocation by the permitted live/retiring link count. [S07 S19 S24]

7. Minimal architectural correction

Retain one authenticated link, one transport Worker, one private main/Worker FIFO, the existing serialized writer, current receive policies and generated schema owners. The fix does not require another socket, a shared-memory payload transport, an async Rust runtime or a general protocol redesign.

Place one authoritative role ledger before the first framework retention. Public FS/auth adapters reserve through this owner before encoding and before readiness waits. WorkerLink and Worker-local HELLO/PING/answer/control producers use the same implementation. A low-level standalone writer gets the same bounded primitive under its own socket owner.

Use fixed-capacity tickets with ledger epoch, slot incarnation, class, byte charge and independent payload/operation retirement flags. Reserve all required units atomically or roll back immediately. Do not allocate a Promise waiter for failed admission. A fixed SPSC handoff may implement the ledger, but shared memory is justified here only by parked-main progress.

After reservation, compact ordinary caller input into exact-size owned storage. Leave caller buffers usable. Price the admitted snapshot, actual message clone and active frame overlap. Reject shared-backed input before dispatch unless an explicit synchronized ownership contract is approved. A transfer list is an optional optimization, not the proof.

Keep payload credit until the last charged transport reference is gone. Keep CALL records until caller settlement, Worker pending/abandoned retirement and retained terminal delivery finish. Worker must update shared credit without waiting for main callbacks; otherwise a blocking caller can deadlock the release.

Reserve handler count and maximum answer bytes before running host-CALL application code. If no reservation fits, follow the approved terminal path before any handler effect. Already-admitted answers consume their existing tickets. Merely failing to enqueue the result after a side effect is too late.

Preserve the existing global FIFO for admitted frames. Use per-producer admission shares if needed. Keep answer/control capacity protected, but do not claim it is priority service. Bound queue residence and graceful close separately; after a partial-write failure poison/close, never skip bytes and continue.

Extend the current Host UI owner with bounded permits that survive mpsc -> Tao -> physical consumer. Do not release at forwarding. A bounded queue plus one coalesced wake is an alternative only if the existing owner keeps the sole ordered payload queue; do not duplicate backlog in two queues.

Bound the native-fact mailbox before filtering. Do not block the native UI waiting for the role. Any coalescing must name exact replaceable state facts and preserve lifecycle/close/created/released semantics. Otherwise overflow is explicit terminal failure, not silent loss.

Add schema-level collection/decoded-storage limits during decoding and budgeted generated encoding. Reuse existing codec and schema generation; never hand-edit generated files or replicate permission validation in the transport.

Add an absolute Rust write deadline and an independent finite renderer response deadline. Make close/cancellation reachable without acquiring the lock held by blocked I/O. Reap completed readers outside the guardian acknowledgement cycle, with a bounded retirement backlog.

Preserve current useful mechanisms: Rust preallocation validation, first-byte receive clock, one outstanding FS admission, Auth tickets through physical drain, fixed ring/reply storage, coalesced KICK, first-terminal-wins state, write poison, generation fences and ordered source disposal. A rewrite that drops those mechanisms is a regression, regardless of language or thread count.

11. Performance and memory measurement methodology
Pin the work and environment

Record commit, source/test hashes, Bun revision, Rust/toolchain, OS/build, architecture, CPU, power state, memory, socket backend, limits, schema, compiler/profile, signing/packaging when relevant, and concurrent machine load. Use identical application effects and payload bytes in baseline and candidate. A native UDS result does not qualify Windows named pipes.
Separate workload classes

Use64B,1KiB,64KiB,1MiB,8MiB and legal16MiB framing payloads, plus mixtures with occasional large frames and many tiny messages. Include zero/minimum records, pooled/subview/shared inputs,1/2/8/32 logical producers, callback-bound work, stalled peer, drip peer, Ready withheld, slow UI and slow handler. Distinguish schema-valid limits from raw framing limits.
Use open and closed load

Closed-loop fixed in-flight tests measure normal service; they hide an overload backlog by self-throttling. Open-loop offered arrivals must use absolute scheduled times and record generator lateness so coordinated omission is visible. Select load levels relative to an independently measured baseline saturation point; do not invent throughput numbers in advance.
Measure the full timeline

Record offered, admitted, encoded, posted, Worker-received, queued, first-write, last-write, Host-read, decoded, dispatched, effect-committed, replied and consumer-retired events keyed by correlation/ticket/generation. Use one monotonic clock for each duration. Do not subtract unrelated process clocks without a clock model. Acceptance latency and consumer completion latency are distinct.
Observe resources independently

Record reserved bytes/counts and independently inspect owned backing sizes, live objects, queue/proxy entries, timer/pending/handler counts, retired reader handles, descriptors and generation overlap. Log logical payload bytes, capacity bytes, allocated bytes, live retained bytes and process RSS/private memory as separate metrics. Include GC/allocator retained capacity and peak overlap; a plateau alone is not a hard bound.
Report statistics honestly

Report offered/admitted/refused/completed rates separately, bytes including or excluding headers explicitly, latency p50/p95/p99/p99.9/max, service/queue-time decomposition, sample counts and run duration. Use repeated independent process runs with randomized baseline/candidate order and confidence intervals. Do not average percentiles into a supposed pooled percentile. Publish raw data and define all exclusions before the run.
Keep instrumentation from deciding the score

Use a traced diagnostic arm for attribution and an equivalent minimally instrumented arm for performance scoring. Quantify instrumentation overhead. Forced GC and WeakRef probes are retention diagnostics, not normal production throughput workloads.
Apply the actual gates

Require no silent drops, exact byte/correlation transcript, bounded independent census, same successful public outcomes, timely overload/terminal behavior, complete cleanup and a healthy successor. Existing architecture targets and the repository regression-review rule remain gates only for the workloads/platforms they define. Do not declare them met from these witnesses.
Keep artifacts reproducible

Retain fixture, payload seed/digests, exact command, mutation patch/hash, complete stdout/stderr/exit, source pin, environment and chronological machine-readable observations. A negative-control suite must name which oracle turned RED and why another guard did not mask it. Store unrun rows as unrun.
12. Implementation sequence and acceptance boundary

First reconcile the architecture contradictions and the current GH623 draft pin. Freeze the local005 branch and overload behavior with the existing owners; make capacity/copy decisions concrete in B1/B2.

Before implementation, turn the supplied witnesses into ordinary target regressions with explicit admitted/refused counts. Add pre-Ready, pending-call, handler-answer and UI-proxy tests so the bound cannot move to an unseen queue.

Implement the shared admission/lifetime primitive and integrate every current producer. Keep source-generation/stamping ownership and existing transport semantics. Add schema/Host/UI corrections in their owning modules; do not hide them behind the outbound counter.

Execute every positive and one-fault negative on the exact candidate. Prove selected-Bun backing behavior, physical termination and platform-specific deadlines. Qualify macOS, Windows named pipes and Linux independently before cross-platform claims.

Measure equivalent-work performance and total resource census. Activate only after B3 and the relevant public API/wire/native gates close. An audit report, passing witness probe or a small logical queue counter is not a production acceptance receipt.

Remaining unknowns are explicit: numeric production limits; exact runtime/native temporary-copy overhead and reclamation timing; full installed-consumer reactions to new synchronous refusal; native short-write timing; physical UI flood/proxy capacity; restart-soak cleanup; and Windows/Linux behavior. Source inspection supports the named paths, not a formal proof that all future plugins or arbitrary application allocations are bounded.
